To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the right number of latent semantic factors (dimensions) to describe a large corpus of text (e.g. the full vocabulary of a natural language) are 300, and the right number of factors to describe an individual's knowledge (e.g. of a natural language vocabulary) are 100.

1. LSA, a general theory of acquired knowledge representation, can be used to successfully simulate many psycholinguistic and other phenomena, 2. LSA can be applied to any body of text to induce a representation of its knowledge, and 3. The LSA representation is a general knowledge representation that can be used for a wide variety of purposes, including natural language understanding,

the right number of latent semantic dimensions (300) is enough to represent the full English vocabulary (about 20,000 words) with high accuracy (about 85%), that the resulting knowledge representation is a powerful and accurate predictor of human performance, that the representation can be learned from text in a few hours, and that the resulting knowledge can be acquired at a rate comparable to human vocabulary learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a general theory of learning and representation of knowledge.
how we learn to represent the world.
the question of what it means for a computer system to know something.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LSA is an empirically successful and theoretically powerful general theory of knowledge representation, acquisition, and induction.
LSA is an extremely powerful, simple, and general mathematical theory of knowledge representation and induction.
LSA is the best current theory of human knowledge representation, induction and acquisition, and the most successful computational model of human knowledge and learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LSA provides the first successful solution to Plato's problem of learning from little information.

we have shown that a simple mathematical model can simulate the acquisition of knowledge in the real world, and that this model is a viable alternative to the current theories of human knowledge representation.

LSA is a general method for acquiring, representing, and reasoning about knowledge, and that it can be used to solve a wide variety of problems, from psycholinguistic to information retrieval to machine learning to knowledge acquisition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the right number of latent dimensions is the number needed to represent the information in the data, not the number of objects or features.
knowledge representation can be learned from text.
knowledge is not stored as a list of facts, nor as a list of features.
